Saturday June 13, 2026 morning. Good morning. The June 13 morning brief opens on the most consequential 48-hour window of the 106-day Hormuz conflict arc — a weekend signing scenario that, if executed, would be the defining geopolitical event of 2026. Pakistani Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif announced on June 12 that negotiators have reached a 'final, agreed-upon text' of a US-Iran peace deal — the first externally confirmed final-text characterization in the conflict's history. Trump followed within hours: 'The strait will officially open as soon as we sign, which could be soon, very soon, maybe over the weekend in Europe.' The operational signal arrived separately: four US Air Force C-17s departed to Europe on June 12, assessed as logistical preparation for a potential Vice President Vance signing ceremony in Geneva. That combination — Pakistani PM final-text confirmation, Trump geographic-temporal commitment, and C-17 advance positioning — constitutes the highest-confidence deal-proximity cluster of the conflict arc. The morning brief's critical complicating entry is the Iranian FM counter-signal: a spokesperson for Iran's foreign ministry stated Friday that Tehran had 'not yet reached a final decision' — a contradiction of the Pakistani PM's final-text framing that introduces signing uncertainty without clearly invalidating the deal text itself. Iranian state media has routinely offered contradictory accounts during the negotiation cycle; Pakistani PM characterizations have a stronger independent-channel track record; but the FM statement makes an unconditional weekend signature less certain than the C-17 signal alone implied. Overnight kinetics: the US military confirmed June 12 intercepts of two Iranian attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz — kinetic activity concurrent with final-text finalization, not resolved by it; the Strait remains closed (Day 106); CENTCOM has issued no stand-down order. Iran comms resolved advances to Day 10 — the longest confirmed-open channel streak of the conflict. PNW situational awareness is at elevated stress ahead of the heat-fire-FIFA convergence now 24 hours out: NWS Portland has issued an Extreme Heat Warning effective tomorrow June 14 through Tuesday June 16 for the Portland-Vancouver Metro, Western Columbia River Gorge, and Chehalem Mountains — temperatures 92-100°F — arriving directly on the FIFA Seattle opener (June 15, Belgium vs Egypt, noon PT at Lumen Field). The noon kickoff at peak heat under the warning is the highest-stress public-event operational scenario of the FIFA Seattle window. FOMC enters the pre-meeting weekend quiet with T-3 to Warsh's inaugural June 16-17 session — 30 days of Warsh silence ends with the June 17 press conference; no pre-meeting communication expected through Sunday, but any signal would carry maximum market weight. Measles updated to 2,073 confirmed cases nationally per CDC June 11 update — the case count is now 215 away from the 2025 full-year record (2,288); summer mobile phase is fully operative; the FIFA Seattle mass-event window starting June 15 is the highest-density transmission-amplification scenario remaining in the US calendar.

vibe.rationale: Vibe 4 — upgraded from Vibe 3 lower edge on the June 12 Pakistani PM 'final, agreed-upon text' announcement and Trump 'weekend in Europe' signing commitment. The C-17 advance logistics positioning to Europe (assessed Vance Geneva ceremony prep) is the morning brief's most operationally specific new signal: executive travel logistics are not activated for a deal that is not imminent. Three factors set the upgrade and three factors hold the ceiling at 4. Upgrade factors: (1) Pakistani PM final-text confirmation — the first externally confirmed statement that negotiators have concluded a final text; qualitatively more specific than all prior 'closing in' / 'broad principles' language; Pakistani PM carries independent-channel credibility as the Islamabad Talks convener distinct from Gulf intermediaries; (2) Trump geographic-temporal commitment — 'weekend in Europe' is the first specific presidential signing window; combined with C-17 logistics positioning, this is the highest-probability near-term signing scenario of the conflict arc; (3) Iran comms resolved Day 10 — longest confirmed-open communication streak of the conflict, suggesting channel integrity held through the finalization phase. Ceiling-at-4 factors: (1) Iran FM contradiction active — 'not yet reached a final decision' introduces credible signing uncertainty; the deal is unsigned and Iranian principal signatory authority (Khamenei) has not been independently confirmed; June 12 kinetic activity (2 drone intercepts) ongoing; Hormuz closed Day 106, no CENTCOM stand-down; (2) FOMC T-3 — weekend pre-meeting quiet begins today; Warsh's inaugural June 16-17 meeting with policy statement bias shift from easing to neutral; 4 April dissents (most divided since 1992); ECB rate hike signal adds external pressure; first press conference calibration under deal-environment uncertainty; (3) PNW heat-fire-FIFA triple convergence 24 hours out — Extreme Heat Warning activates tomorrow; 92-100°F landing on FIFA Seattle opener June 15 noon PT; east Cascades above-normal fire ignition risk elevated by heat; NIFC-FIFA co-response Day 6 at its first high-intensity dual-mandate test. Upgrade to 5 requires: confirmed US-Iran signing in Europe; Hormuz reopening timeline activated; CENTCOM stand-down issued. Drop to 3 requires: Trump deal-text rejection or major Iranian counter-demand; new confirmed escalation; FOMC weekend signal triggering bond market dislocation; major PNW ignition concurrent with heat wave.

Pakistani Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif announced June 12 that negotiators have reached a 'final, agreed-upon text' of a US-Iran peace deal — the first externally confirmed final-text characterization of the conflict. Trump followed within hours with the first specific geographic and temporal commitment: 'The strait will officially open as soon as we sign, which could be soon, very soon, maybe over the weekend in Europe.' The operational signal that distinguishes this cycle from prior deal-proximity language: four US Air Force C-17 transport aircraft departed to Europe on June 12, assessed as logistical preparation for a potential Vice President Vance signing ceremony in Geneva in the coming days. Executive travel logistics at that scale — aircraft, advance teams, site preparation — are not activated for a speculative deal. The MOU framework as described includes Iran's commitment not to pursue nuclear weapons; a permanent halt to all hostilities including Lebanon; Hormuz reopening within 30 days of signing; and a 60-day follow-on window for nuclear program specifics. The morning brief's critical complicating signal: a spokesperson for Iran's foreign ministry stated that Tehran had 'not yet reached a final decision' — a direct contradiction of the Pakistani PM's final-text framing. Iranian state media and FM statements have routinely diverged from third-party channel characterizations throughout the negotiation cycle; the Iranian FM has historically trailed behind back-channel progress by 24-48 hours. However, the contradiction cannot be dismissed as routine — it introduces uncertainty about whether Khamenei has formally authorized the final text. The overnight kinetic environment confirms the deal remains unsigned: the US military intercepted two Iranian attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz on June 12 after Iranian forces reportedly fired on a transiting vessel; no vessel was confirmed struck; the Strait remains closed (Day 106); CENTCOM has issued no stand-down order. Iran comms resolved Day 10 — longest confirmed-open streak of the conflict, supporting the argument that back-channel coordination is intact despite FM contradictions. items.summary: The June 13 morning economic picture is dominated by the three-day FOMC countdown entering the pre-meeting weekend quiet window. Warsh's inaugural June 16-17 meeting is the most anticipated single Federal Reserve event of the year — markets are pricing 98.3% probability of no rate move; the hold is near-certain. The signal is in the statement language: the June meeting is expected to mark an explicit shift from an easing bias to a neutral stance, reflecting May CPI 4.2% YoY (highest since April 2023), core 2.9%, and nominal spending 5.9% QoQ annualized (roughly 1.9 points above the ~4% pace consistent with 2% inflation). The April FOMC produced 4 dissents — most divided committee since 1992 — creating elevated drafting complexity for Warsh's first statement. Warsh has been silent for 30 days since confirmation; the June 17 press conference ends that silence and is the primary market-signal event of the cycle — the language of neutrality vs. tightening bias will set late-2026 rate expectations (CME pricing ~70% hike odds for late 2026). The pre-meeting quiet window runs Saturday-Sunday (June 13-14); no Fed communications expected through the weekend. An external pressure has entered the weekend calculus: the ECB rate hike signal, if executed, could force a reassessment of the Fed's relative monetary policy posture at precisely the moment Warsh is attempting to define his tenure's parameters. The Brent crude picture introduces weekend volatility risk into the FOMC framework: the Pakistani PM final-text signal has eased Brent into the $90-95 range (Hormuz-within-30-days clause is a structural ceiling signal if confirmed), but the Iran FM 'not yet a final decision' contradiction creates intraday volatility exposure as markets assess weekend signing probability. Warsh's inaugural statement will almost certainly be drafted without knowing whether the ~40% YoY energy contribution to CPI will collapse or persist — the deal-uncertainty variable enters the Fed's June 16 opening deliberations directly.

NWS Portland has issued the Extreme Heat Warning effective June 14 through June 16 — 92-100°F, overnight lows 63-67°F — for the Portland-Vancouver Metro, Western Columbia River Gorge, and Chehalem Mountains. Seattle's June 15 match (noon PT kickoff under the warning window) places full-capacity attendance under direct-sun conditions at the highest heat level Seattle typically sees in any given June. Gates open four hours before kickoff (8:00 AM PT) under what will already be rising heat; venue medical staff and Seattle OEM are the primary public health response agencies for the inaugural Lumen Field match. Let's Play SEA 26 at Seattle Center advances to Day 3 — open-air fan activation under the same heat warning level; Seattle Center has no air conditioning; cooling center activation and hydration protocol deployment ahead of Sunday onset are the Day 3 primary operational watch items. Security posture: SEAR-2 designation; $32M FEMA grant; CCTV cameras operational (Day 3 FIFA active); drone restrictions around Lumen Field. Shamkhani IRGC cyber risk Day 19 concurrent with FIFA hacktivist window Day 3 — CISA clean streak Day 42; FBI IC3 no flash in overnight cycle. NIFC-FIFA co-response fully active Day 6: the June 14-16 heat event is the first high-intensity test of both the wildfire suppression resource allocation mandate and the FIFA mass-event security mandate simultaneously. Sound Transit's $34.5B funding gap remains unresolved T-2 to first match; Link Light Rail is the primary Lumen Field transit mode; first-match load test under heat warning conditions is the highest operational complexity scenario of the gap period. Measles amplification risk: 2,073 national cases, summer mobile phase, FIFA mass gatherings across consecutive days — the June 15 opener is the peak risk window.

items.summary: Four secondary PNW environmental and civic threads entering June 13 morning. First: PNW fire-drought conditions are at their most advanced since the NIFC above-normal period opened. The east Cascades are explicitly above normal in the June NIFC outlook; the east-slope fire onset target of July is T-17 days; the arrival of the June 14-16 heat event (92-100°F) is the most significant fuel-drying acceleration since the NIFC above-normal period began. Three days of heat at that level will advance soil moisture deficit, eliminate any remaining east-slope snowmelt moisture advantage, and accelerate grass and shrub fuel curing on the Columbia Plateau and east Cascades foothills toward early-July ignition conditions. No overnight ignitions reported; the pre-dawn June 13 window is the last lowest-risk period before the heat event accelerates the ignition timeline. Oregon drought at 83% coverage (12 counties emergency); Washington statewide drought emergency Day 9 (4th consecutive year); snowpack at roughly half of normal; El Nino 61% summer probability; Super El Nino 1-in-4 (temperature anomaly amplifier). Oregon wildfire season expected severe, lasting into October. Second: NSF Newport OR ocean observatory (last remaining PNW floating offshore station) continues advancing toward end-of-June removal — approximately two weeks out. The station is operational for the June 14-16 heat event, providing the atmospheric river early detection and marine heat wave monitoring that will be unavailable after removal. The heat event arriving now illustrates exactly what the monitoring network loses when the station goes dark in approximately two weeks. Third: Oregon gray whale washups continue at 21 YTD (Oregon coast), 17 YTD (Washington), above expected annual pace — serious emaciation consistent with Pacific prey availability collapse; ocean monitoring network dismantlement concurrent with marine ecosystem stress represents the PNW's ongoing science infrastructure deficit. Fourth: Portland's heat emergency protocol is activating ahead of Sunday onset — cooling centers deploying, vulnerable population outreach active; the city's 2021 heat dome experience (1,000+ Oregon deaths) defines the baseline response framework; no heat-related mortality or injury in the overnight cycle.

analyst_summary: June 13, 2026 morning opens at Vibe 4 — upgraded from Vibe 3 lower edge on the strength of the June 12 deal-proximity cluster: Pakistani PM 'final, agreed-upon text' announcement, Trump 'weekend in Europe' geographic-temporal commitment, and four C-17 aircraft departed to Europe in assessed advance positioning for a Vance Geneva signing ceremony. These represent the highest-confidence deal-proximity cluster of the 106-day Hormuz conflict arc. The morning brief's critical complication is the Iran FM counter-signal: Tehran's foreign ministry spokesperson said Iran had 'not yet reached a final decision,' introducing signing uncertainty without clearly invalidating the deal text. The Hormuz closure (Day 106), naval blockade (Day 63), and kinetic activity (June 12 dual drone intercepts) remain fully operative; CENTCOM has issued no stand-down. Weekend watch items are concentrated in four domains: (1) Deal signature signal — the weekend Europe window is open; a confirmed signing transforms the geopolitical, market, energy, and domestic political picture simultaneously; Trump deal-text editing and the Iran FM contradiction are the primary delay risks; Brent direction ($88-92 on signature vs $97-105+ on collapse) is the fastest proxy; (2) PNW overnight ignitions and heat onset — the June 14 heat warning activation is T-24 hours; east Cascades above-normal fuel conditions make any June 13-14 overnight ignition a potential NIFC-FIFA co-response dual-mandate conflict; (3) FIFA Seattle June 15 opener — Belgium vs Egypt, noon PT, 92-100°F, Lumen Field open-air; venue medical capacity, heat-related incident monitoring, and CISA cyber clean streak Day 42 are the primary June 14-15 watch items; (4) FOMC pre-meeting quiet — Warsh inaugural June 16-17 meeting; any weekend signal carries maximum market weight; statement bias shift from easing to neutral is the first concrete Warsh policy move.
